What are the most important qualities should one look for in a firearm used for defense in a SHTF situation?

1) Weight and size of the firearm

2) Scarcity of ammunition

3) Size of caliber

4) Ease of cleaning and disassembly

5) Reliability

I love my Yugo SKS. I do compromise on weight a little for the benefits of the other qualities.

Each situation is its own. What would you add or subtract from this list? What do you have in your arsenal? Is it necessary to have multiple types of firearms (shotgun, rifle, handgun) or will one gun suffice?

The Yugo has a 7.62 round, which is high recoil, lousy for autofire and heavy.

It's also not as abundantly available as a 5.56, which is great for autofire and light.

The age old argument that 5.56 doesn't have enough stopping power has been proven wrong by all military missions in the last 20 years.

I'd probably pick a SCAR 16S in the 5.56 caliber for short to medium range.

For long range I'd go with a .300WSM, maybe a Winchester model 70.

In SHTF, CQB might become a factor too, I'd add that to your list think.

Yes, CQB is a factor I didn't consider, thanks for raising that point. The SKS is also limited by the 10 round internal box magazine. I could put one of those Norinco mags on it but I've read that they are of very poor quality. Also, I'm pretty broke, haha... When I get some money saved up, my next rifle is going to be an AR15 in 5.56 or a bolt-action .30-06 or .308. In terms of pistols Glock 22 or Springfield XD in .40 will be my next pistol purchase.

If you do get a bolt action, read up on the 300WSM.

It's an amazing round, and unless you NEED a 30-06 for some reason, the 300WSM actually has more applications, is faster, has a flatter trajectory and is lighter on recoil.

For hand guns I'm a SIG fanboy, the P226 would be my pick, but it's hella expensive.

My wallet-choice would be a Glock 17 over the 22, as the 22's .40 round has not become widely adapted and therefore doesn't adhere to the criterium of scarcity of ammo.

A 1911 would be nice too, those are indestructible!

Though I don't have a firearm, I'm well familiar with them from having grown up in the country. That said, I'd personally probably go with a .22 of some sort if I had a choice. Ammunition's dirt-cheap comparatively, plentiful, and would still put a hole in something in a self-defense situation, I'm sure at least enough to cause confusion.

Personally though, I'd rather have a high-quality slingshot. A steel ball-bearing or small rock launched by a few tubes of surgical tubing is still going to do a lot. And ammo is basically infinite.

IAMA: 24 y/o woman from Sweden with Borderline personality disorder with a self-harm addiction who has been to psych-ward 30+ times, ask away!
Aside from all the psychobabble mumbo jumbo definitions, how would you yourself describe your disorder so that it reflects how it affects you on a daily basis?

I have terrible moodswings, I have periods of depression. Self-harm is the biggest thing affecting me, even though I rarely do it anymore.

I can give you an example of an event that is completely trivial to others but at the point made me want to kill myself:

I had a tomato plant on my balcony and needed to trim it a bit, I got so caught up in it that I trimmed it down to the stem and two twigs. After that I had a panic attack and cried for 2 hours because I had almost killed my tomato plant.

This might seem ridiculous but to me it was dead serious. The intensiveness of emotions are the hardest part to deal with.

As someone battling depression, I don't think it's ridiculous at all.

I'm sometimes overcome by my emotions, and even though I know what's happening, can't do a thing about it.

Fortunately I don't have the instant mood swings, that must be pretty hard to deal with, like being on a rollercoaster.

After all this time, have you learned any coping mechanisms, or does it completely dictate your existence?

I do have coping mechanisms such as medicine, a psychologist and various "tools" I use when I get panic attacks or start feeling very depressed. I have been able to learn how to break an impulse and think before I act, most of the times, as well as handling mood swings.
How has the personality disorder affected your life with your family and friends?

My family has been nothing but supportive to me. My mum stayed home for around 8 years to take care of me while I was at my worst. She would stay up all night and day to make sure I did not try to commit suicide or self harm. I am best friends with my little brother, who still lives with my parents and they all live on the same street as me.

Friends have not been a problem I have 3 very close friends 2 girls I met in high-school and a guy who used to work at psych ward while I was there, I later found out we had friends in common and we started hanging out. Most of my friends have or have had problems with mental illness themselves and they are supportive just as I am supportive to them.

I have always striven to get better even at my worst and I think that has been the reason my family and friends have tolerated and helped me with my mood swings, depression and self harm.

That is not an easy life that you are describing. What is it that you do apart from struggling with your healt? Do you study or work? How has this been going on? Many greetings from the other side of the baltic sea :)

Right now Im on welfare/get a pension because Im to sick to work. I have finished high-school and I have been doing some internships/volunteering at different places to get some structure and a taste of work-life. Sadly I have been getting worse lately, had a real nasty depression period, stomach issues and at times I have been hallucinating . So right now Im just trying to get back on my feet.
That sounds like a tough struggle. I know depression is a real hard condition to get rid of. Does such online communication help you? Does it make you better in some way?
Online communities helps alot, as well as the support from my bf, friends and family. Just having someone to talk to does alot.
I've been to Sweden once, to Karlskrona. There is a ferry from Gdynia. Sweden seems really enjoyable place to live. You travel a bit?
I've been to London 3 times, love it. Otherwise I've been to Denmark and Germany, only with the ferry.

Hi! Thanks for doing this AMA

I recently been to the psych ward due to depression/sucial thoughts brought on with my addiction to pain killers. Im curious to what kind of treatment you have been given and if you were given a medical diagnosis? I ask because from what i seen was pretty much just like jail only better food. Also with the bonus of a shot of harmadol (sp?) If you act up or refuse to take your medication if you are deemed incompetent. So im curious as to what kind of medical treatment is provided. Thanks

Also are you literally scared of rabbits or people in evil bunny costumes?

Psych ward in Sweden is mostly storage, they make sure you don't kill yourself, harm yourself or others and that you take your pills. Some of the staff were wonderful helpful ppl but most of them were assholes.

I started seeing a psychologist when I was 13, still seeing one, and when I was 14 I was hospitalized for the first time for a suicide attempt. I have been on a cocktail of different anti-depressant, mood stabilizers, anti-psychotics(neuroleptica), sleeping pills and sedatives.

I got my diagnosis: Borderline Personality Disorder, 2 months before my 18th birthday and it has been re diagnosed 2-3 times after that.

Right now Im on 2 different anti-depressants, 1 mood-stabilizer that I have been taking since I was 15, sleeping pills also taken since I was 15 and Valium in case I have panic attacks.

I have been restrained at psych-ward so many times I lost count and I have been given an injection, not hamadol but similar, 2 or 3 times.

Only actual living rabbits scare me not pics of them, not ppl in bunny suits etc.

Ok so sounds like psyc wards and sweden and florida usa are the same. What is your opinion about anti depressant and mood stabalizer medication? I ask because i personally believe all that crap makss any one person worse off. They tried giving me that stuff but i refused. They can all kiss my ass.

I have tried being without and I cant. Although Im perfectly aware of all the awful side effects. Its different for everyone some ppl need them some don't. I do think pharmaceutical companies need to develop better medicine with less side effects.
Has joining an online community helped you in any way?
Joining reddits self-harm sub and its tinychat has helped me cope with the recent difficulties.
I think it's great you're doing this AMA, and I hope it will help in giving you the feeling people are out there for you when you need them!
I did a few casual ama's at reddit a few months ago. I just like spreading the word and educate on mental illness.
How are your romantic relationships, has it been a struggle to maintain those types of relationships or do you find a way?

I have been with my bf for 8 years now. We have had a tough time, I have been confused, angry and wanting to break up in the heat of the moment a few times. I feel like I should be honest so here it goes I slept with a girl, who was my friend at the time, while I was with my bf. We had an understanding that I could kiss and touch other girls since im bisexual but i took it to far and I told him right after it happened. He forgave me. It has never happened again.

I know alot of ppl will hate me for being a cheater but its so hard to controll impulses and when you have been drinking and smoking weed it gets even harder.

Today we have a healthy relationship and we are discussing having a baby in the near future. He has Asperger syndrome so he is like the complete opposite of me, logic and methodical, but we make it work. I was 16 and he was 17 when we got together and its been one hell of a run, I love him more than I have loved anyone else and I think we will be one of those couples that stay together 50+ years.
Thanks for opening up, I wish you and your partner many years of health and happiness!

That's really awesome. I was going to ask the question whether you could love someone else (and be loved in return) because I have a sister who had a psychotic break 3 years ago and wonder if she will ever meet someone. Or it could be that my sister is really annoying...who knows.

I was sad to read about what you are having to deal with. I was heartened that you have such support! I think but for that things would be very different for you now. Kudos to your friends and family - lucky might not be a good word to use, but I am very glad you have such a supportive environment. Good luck lady! I hope you find sustainable happiness.
Thank you for that it really warmed my heart :)
Is it free to go to the psych ward in Sweden??

Until you turn 20 all healthcare is free psych ward included. After that you pay approximately 8 dollars a day, while you are committed, and it has a max of around 100-200 then you dont have to pay anything for a year or 6 months (cant remember exactly) no matter which hospital ward you get committed to.

That's is so awesome. Most homeless people in my area of the U.S. Are mentally ill. I've often wondered if decreasing the price of a stay in a psych ward would help at least get them off the street. Is that a problem in Sweden too?

Most homeless ppl in Sweden are drug-addicts or alcoholics. I live in one of the biggest city's in Sweden, population approximately 1 million, and there are around 300 Swedish citizens that are homeless and actually live on the streets here.

In recent years we have had an influx of homeless Romanians and Romano(gypsies), EU decided you are free to move to any country that is a member of EU, and they are homeless living in shacks, caravans and tents begging for a living.
How do your friends deal with this? Do they help at all?

My friends all have some form of mental illness themselves so they know what it is like. We talk, we hug, we cry, they visit me when I cant leave my apartment due to social anxiety, they visit me if I go to the hospital etc.

We do normal stuff to, one of my best friends loves movies as do I and we usually gather to watch new movies with a couple of other friends. All in all normal best friend relationship with extra support during rough times.
Why are you also scared of bunnies? Also what advice would you give for people who are around you when things get bad and want to help, or is there nothing they can do?

Because they always kick and scratch they are totally unreliable if they get spooked you get claw kicked. Also some of them bite, and have you seen how much they poop? The poop factor is scary by itself.

Try to talk calmly, don't panic or I will panic even more, hugs and touching (like rubbing a shoulder or my back) helps to. Just be there and try to listen to what I say, if I say something.

Thanks for the advice I would have thought hugs and touching could just make things worse.. But maybe not!

If it helps I don't really bunnies them either.. Better bunnies than bees though.
Its different for different ppl but touching calms me down a bit and makes me feel safe.
I guess that makes sense, it's different for everyone, thanks for the advice!

What are the words that you want to hear most when you're depressed or ready to self harm?

My brother has been suffering from a less serious condition, but still has serious depression and anxiety. He has self harmed a couple times. I've always worried about coming home to something I don't want to see.

Tell him you love him and that you will always be there, he doesn't have to talk to you, you can just hug him :)

Its nice to have company and not have to talk about it all the time.
